title: Amazon API Gateway to AWS Step Functions Express to Amazon Athena
description: Run an Amazon Athena query through an AWS Step Functions Express Workflow and return the rows in one synchronous Amazon API Gateway call, with no Lambda function.

introBox.headline: How it works
text: This pattern runs an Amazon Athena query and returns its rows in one synchronous Amazon API Gateway request. The REST API starts an AWS Step Functions Express Workflow with `StartSyncExecution`, and the workflow calls Athena through native service integrations, so there's no AWS Lambda function in the request path.

Express Workflows don't support the `.sync` integration pattern, so the workflow starts the query with `StartQueryExecution` and polls `GetQueryExecution` in a `Wait` and `Choice` loop. When the query succeeds, `GetQueryResults` reads the rows, which must fit in the 256 KiB Step Functions payload. After 10 polls the workflow calls `StopQueryExecution` and fails, so the caller gets an HTTP 500 before the 29-second integration timeout.

The method uses IAM authorization, because the caller's SQL goes straight to Athena, and the stage is throttled to 5 requests per second. Athena reads a sample CSV file through an AWS Glue table and writes results to an Amazon S3 prefix set by its workgroup.

bullets.text: Call Amazon Athena with AWS Step Functions

text: Send a SigV4-signed POST with a queryString to the ApiEndpoint output, for example with curl --aws-sigv4. See the README in the GitHub repo for the commands.
Delete the stack: cd apigw-sfn-athena/typescript/cdk/cdk then npx cdk destroy.
Warning: this deletes the Amazon S3 bucket and all sample data and Amazon Athena query results.
